instruction: Execute this ordered task: (1) ONLY the physical right arm picks up the capped transparent plastic bottle containing amber liquid, places it upright ON the black plastic support, releases it and verifies it stands there. (2) The right arm regrips the bottle, returns it upright to its original tabletop location, releases it and withdraws clear. (3) ONLY then the physical left arm picks up the tennis ball from the tabletop, places it on the now-empty black plastic support, releases it, verifies the ball stays there, and withdraws clear. Finish with both arms powered and stationary. Verify every placement after opening the jaws. Do not declare done after merely lifting an object.
content: This is a NEW task with changed objects and positions. The earlier red cola can is absent. The right target is the transparent, white-capped plastic bottle containing amber liquid. The black hollow plastic support is the shared destination. The ball now rests on the TABLE, not on the support. Previous successful ball grasp coordinates cannot be replayed at this lower height. The supplied reference photo records the initial bottle location for its round trip; current live images always determine obstacles and clearance.

content.label: INITIAL SCENE REFERENCE: preserve the bottle's original tabletop location for its return; this is not a live camera frame

content: Physical arm identity is unchanged: right=can1=right wrist image, left=can0=left wrist image. In the shared external image named top, physical right and bottle appear on SCREEN LEFT; physical left and tennis appear on SCREEN RIGHT. top is an oblique RGB view, not calibrated overhead geometry. Each arm has its own base frame. Reference image pixels are not base coordinates. Do not transfer signs or absolute targets between arms.

Run one arm at a time. During all bottle stages, left must be null in every arm/gripper tool. After the bottle is returned, released, and right has withdrawn from the shared support corridor, keep right null while left handles the tennis ball. Never bring both hands into the shared support area together. The host opens the initially empty jaws before model decisions.

Maintain explicit progress: prefix each action note with its stage (bottle pickup, bottle placement, bottle return, or tennis placement) and mention the last visually verified milestone. Record the actual bottle pickup/release TCP pose and orientation before transporting it, so the return has a reference, but reacquire images and verify its original tabletop footprint rather than blindly replaying coordinates. Preserve the bottle upright and the cap closed. Place means the object is supported and the gripper is released; hovering over the support is not placement.

Grasp lesson: the fingers must actually straddle the object at suitable contact height with enough insertion depth. Projected wrist centering alone repeatedly caused empty grasps. Use the global image for height and distance, and the wrist image for inner finger clearance. On this R5, blindly lowering with a fixed reset wrist orientation previously produced poorly tracked negative J3 requests; changing approach and a modest wrist pitch helped. Use measured J1..J6, command poses and residuals to judge actual response. Do not repeatedly force a refused or poorly tracked descent.

The previous can approach was obstructed by the rim dominating the wrist image and the camera housing approaching it. Account for the entire fingers and camera housing around this taller bottle. Keep the plastic bottle from tipping or crushing; raw position is not force sensing. Once a grasp is supported by images, make a short test lift and verify separation from the table before any lateral transport. If the object stays on the table, reopen and choose a meaningfully different alignment instead of repeating lifts.

For placement, inspect the black support top and recess and confirm a stable footprint for the entire bottle base. Carry the object clear of the table and support rim without hitting the idle arm, camera, cables or other object. Align over the destination, lower in bounded stages until supported, then open within the reported gripper_next_opening_bounds. Observe the object remains stationary and upright after release before withdrawing or regripping. Do not release above an edge, balance on one corner, press the object into the support, or infer support from a hidden contact region. Use a supported alternative viewpoint if needed.

After the bottle returns to its initial table location, the black support must be empty and right withdrawn before the left arm proceeds. The ball is on the table now; use open fingers, account for tabletop clearance, and do not push it away while descending. The final goal is the released ball stably on the support and the released bottle at its original location. After verification, hold empty grippers clear; no automatic reset or further opening is needed.

Use original GPT-Policy move_to/move_eef_chunk/check_path/set_gripper with concise decisions and fresh observations. Preserve existing motion, tracking and observation-age checks. Use useful centimetre-scale corrections only on clearly clear paths, smaller near contact. Budget renewal continues the same task and must not erase progress or change the bottle return reference. A hardware fault, person entering the path, unstable support or camera obstruction requires holding/reassessment, never blind continuation. An accepted path or gripper feedback is not proof of physical task success.
